newsitem.title: USA: Knight-Ridder annual mtg draws labor protest.
newsitem.headline: Knight-Ridder annual mtg draws labor protest.

text.p: Knight-Ridder Inc held its annual shareholder meeting here today amid tight security prompted by the presence of vocal labor unionist protesting the company's alleged unfair labor practices at the Detroit Free Press.
While the formal adgenda of the meeting was carried out without incident, Philadelphia-area Teamsters conducted a vocal picket outside.
A Philadelphia police spokesman was not immediately available to describe the size of the crowd, which the union put at 600 to 700 people.
Inside the meeting at the Bellevue Hotel, union activists aired their views in a strictly-timed question-and-answer period.

While Knight-Ridder Chairman Anthony Ridder declined to say specifically what he would do to end the strike in response to questions, he told shareholders that he expects the Free Press to contribute a profit to the corporation in 1997.
A union labor strike began there in July 1995 and was recently called off by the unions.
But Knight-Ridder and the newspaper's organized labor remain locked in rancorous dispute over the return of striking workers and backpay.
In 1996, Ridder said, the Free Press incurred a "significantly reduced loss" versus the $40 - $50 million the strike cost Knight-Ridder in 1995.
"We do not intend to fire replacement workers. The integrity of the Free Press has not been compromised," Ridder said.
